rules.title: Iterators and chunked I/O for large data
rules.what: Process large sequences and files with iterators, generators and chunked reads; avoid building full lists or repeated DataFrame copies in memory.
rules.why: A list doubles the data in memory (objects plus list overhead) and forces the whole dataset through the CPU before the first output; a generator produces the first result immediately at constant memory.
rules.how: Generator expressions over list comprehensions where the result is consumed once; csv/iter chunking for files; DataFrame operations that avoid copies (inplace where safe, views over copies).

patterns.note: Whole-file load; candidate if the file is unbounded or user-supplied.
List comprehension; candidate if the source grows and the result is consumed once.

verify.how: Processing a dataset larger than memory completes with bounded RSS.

limits: Small collections: readability wins; the rule targets data that grows.

rules.title: Vectorise only after profiling
rules.what: Move hot numeric loops to vectorised libraries (numpy/pandas) only after profiling shows they are hot; do not rewrite Python code from a language stereotype.
rules.why: A vectorised rewrite of cold code adds a dependency and readability cost for nothing; of hot code it can yield orders of magnitude. The profile decides which case you are in.
rules.how: Profile (cProfile, py-spy), confirm the hot loop, then vectorise or move to a native extension; keep the profile with the change.

verify.how: Profiles before/after on the same workload ship with the change.

rules.title: No N+1 with the ORM
rules.what: Django/SQLAlchemy access avoids lazy-relation loads inside loops: use select_related (joins), prefetch_related (batches) or explicit IN queries.
rules.why: Accessing obj.rel inside a loop over N objects issues N+1 queries - the most common Django performance defect, invisible in the code and obvious in the query log.
rules.how: select_related for many-to-one/one-to-one, prefetch_related for many-to-many/reverse, .only()/.values() for projections, bulk_create/bulk_update for writes; assert with assertNumQueries.

patterns.note: Loop over an ORM queryset; verify no relation access inside the body.

verify.how: assertNumQueries (or equivalent) shows a constant query count as the row count grows.

rules.title: Bound multiprocessing and close resources
rules.what: Bound worker/queue/process counts to the machine profile; use context managers for files, connections and locks without exception.
rules.why: Unbounded multiprocessing exhausts memory and thrashes the CPU on one machine while appearing 'parallel'; an unclosed resource leaks until the process dies.
rules.how: Pool sizes from the core/RAM budget, with-statement everywhere a resource is acquired, concurrent.futures with bounded executors.

patterns.note: Pool with default or very large size; check machine budget.
Bare open() assignment; verify a close or a with-statement.

verify.how: Worker count under load stays within the bound; fd count stable across iterations (lsof/ulimit check).

rules.title: Don't ship a framework for a script
rules.what: A script or small CLI uses the standard library; no web framework, no DI container, no heavy dependency for a task stdlib covers.
rules.why: Dependencies on a short-lived script are pure import cost: startup time, supply-chain surface, install weight - paid on every run for features never used.
rules.how: argparse/typing/dataclasses/httpx-or-stdlib for scripts; a framework enters when the service grows, not before.

verify.how: Script dependencies each name the stdlib gap they close.

limits: Team conventions may mandate a framework even for small tools; record it as the reason.

rules.title: Async without blocking
rules.what: In asyncio code, no blocking calls on the event loop: no time.sleep, no sync requests, no sync file I/O in coroutines; use the async counterparts or offload.
rules.why: One blocking call freezes every coroutine sharing the loop: the service's whole concurrency collapses on a single slow function.
rules.how: asyncio.sleep, async HTTP clients (httpx/aiohttp), loop.run_in_executor/to_thread for unavoidable blocking work.

patterns.note: time.sleep inside an async function; asyncio.sleep intended.
Sync requests call inside async code; candidate for an async client.

verify.how: Concurrency test: a slow operation does not delay unrelated coroutines beyond budget.

limits: CPU-bound blocking work goes to executors, not async awaits.

rules.title: Vectorise pandas instead of iterating rows
rules.what: Express DataFrame work as column operations; avoid iterrows(), itertuples() loops and apply(axis=1) on large frames.
rules.why: Row iteration runs Python code once per row, where a vectorised operation runs native code once per column: orders of magnitude more CPU for the same result.
rules.how: df['total'] = df['qty'] * df['price']; np.where/np.select for conditions; merge instead of per-row lookups; profile first on small frames.

patterns.note: Row-wise pandas operation; candidate on large frames.

verify.how: Timing on a representative frame before/after, recorded with the change.

rules.title: Sets for membership, join for strings
rules.what: Test membership in a set or dict rather than a large list inside loops, and build strings with ''.join() or io.StringIO instead of += in loops.
rules.why: x in list is linear: inside a loop the work turns quadratic. += on str copies the accumulated text at each step.
rules.how: seen = set(ids) before the loop; parts.append(s) then ''.join(parts).

patterns.note: String accumulated with += inside a loop.

verify.how: No linear membership test over a growing list inside a loop; no str += in loops over data.

rules.title: Reuse HTTP sessions, stream large bodies
rules.what: Make repeated HTTP calls through one requests.Session/httpx.Client with timeouts; stream large uploads and downloads instead of reading them whole.
rules.why: Module-level requests.get opens a new connection each time: DNS and TLS handshake repeated per call. An unbounded .content or read() loads the whole payload into memory.
rules.how: with requests.Session() as s: s.get(url, timeout=(3, 10)); stream=True + iter_content(chunk_size=...) for large bodies.

patterns.note: Module-level requests call inside a loop: no connection reuse.

verify.how: Repeated calls go through a shared session; large bodies are streamed.

rules.title: Bounded memoisation
rules.what: Give caches a bound: lru_cache with a maxsize sized to the working set, never maxsize=None or @cache on functions with unbounded argument space.
rules.why: An unbounded memo cache keeps every distinct argument forever: memory grows with traffic until the process is restarted.
rules.how: @lru_cache(maxsize=1024); cachetools.TTLCache for data that goes stale; cache_info() to check the hit rate.

patterns.note: Unbounded memoisation; acceptable only for a small, closed argument space.

verify.how: cache_info() hit rate and size checked under a representative workload.

limits: @lru_cache() without arguments is bounded (maxsize=128) and is not flagged.

rules.title: No sleep-and-poll loops
rules.what: Do not wait for state changes with while True + time.sleep; react to events (queues, notifications, webhooks) or bound the polling with a timeout and backoff.
rules.why: A polling loop spends CPU and I/O on its own schedule whether or not anything changed and keeps the machine awake.
rules.how: queue.get(timeout=...), watchdog/inotify for files, LISTEN/NOTIFY for databases; otherwise exponential backoff with a deadline.

patterns.note: Infinite loop with sleep: polling candidate.

verify.how: The loop has an event source, or a documented interval, deadline and backoff.
